title: DTG purpose definition
description: The definition of one version of one purpose of use: a code naming what a party may use data it obtains for. A purpose IRI is what a Human Context Protocol grant carries as a purpose `code` (HCP 2.0 §6.1.5.2), what a VTI access-control entry or a DTG VAC lists in `purposes` (VTI-ACL-109; DTG Credentials Core, Purposes of Use), and what a request names when it declares its purpose. It is compared byte-exact, never resolved at use. The members state what using data for the purpose covers and what it does not, the description a person is shown before approving it, and how it relates to purpose names defined elsewhere. Tokens in braces are replaced with the registry's own values when this schema is published.

id.description: The purpose IRI: <purposeNamespace><name>/<version>, in NFC, no trailing slash. The registry build checks it against the folder path and the configured purpose namespace. This exact string is the HCP purpose `code` and the value listed in VTI or VAC `purposes`.

since.description: Date of the release that made this version non-draft. Required from candidate onward.

label.description: A short human name for the purpose.

description.description: One plain-language sentence a person is shown before approving a grant for this purpose: the `description` HCP 2.0 §6.1.5.2 pairs with each purpose code. An authorization service MAY show this text in place of a client-supplied description for the same code.

definition.description: What using data for this purpose means: the normative statement of the use a party declares when it names this purpose.

includes.description: Uses this purpose covers, each stated so a reviewer can decide whether a given use falls under it.

excludes.description: Uses this purpose explicitly does not cover, typically because another purpose names them. A grant for this purpose is not a grant for any of these.

examples.description: Concrete, informative examples of a use declared under this purpose. Example documents that carry the IRI (an HCP authorization detail, a VAC) go in the version folder's examples/ directory.

mappings.description: Informative relations to purpose names and codes defined elsewhere: a VTI Appendix H name, a Data Privacy Vocabulary purpose, a Personal Data Portability Protocol code. SKOS mapping relations, read from this purpose to the other term. Like seeAlso, they are for the people configuring a system; a verifier never treats a mapped term as equal to this IRI on the strength of a mapping (VTI-ACL-109 compares purposes as exact strings), and a system that accepts both maps one to the other in its own configuration.

term.description: The other term exactly as it is written where it is defined: a registered name such as `taskExecution`, or an absolute IRI.

relation.description: The SKOS mapping relation from this purpose to the term: broadMatch means the term is broader than this purpose.

definedIn.description: Where the purpose's normative text lives, if outside this registry.

governedBy.description: Null for this registry's own vocabulary. For a community purpose, the governance framework that defines it.

supersedes.description: The predecessor version, or a community purpose this one is the convergence successor of.

convergenceRecord.description: Required when 'supersedes' names an IRI outside this namespace: the commit or pull request in the community's repository that marks its purpose superseded by this one.

seeAlso.description: Informative pointers. Verifiers never follow these.

languageMap.description: Language-tagged strings. English is required; add every language the defining community uses.
